docRequirement: memory.md:386 binds the WRITE path of the auto-memory index: after Claude writes to `MEMORY.md`, Claude Code measures the file against the 200-line and 25KB read limits. Near a limit it returns a reminder to shorten it ("keep one line per entry, move detail into topic files, and merge or drop stale entries"); over a limit "the write still succeeds, but Claude Code returns an error telling Claude to rewrite the index, because everything past the limit is dropped on the next load". errors.md:1435-1447 gives that error's literal shape ("this write left the memory index at MEMORY.md at 214 lines, over its 200-line read limit. The write succeeded, but everything past the limit is silently dropped each time the index is loaded … Rewrite it to under 140 lines now") and states it is delivered to Claude after the write, not printed as a terminal banner. memory.md:388 / errors.md:1443 narrow WHAT is measured: YAML frontmatter and block-level HTML comments are stripped before the index loads and are therefore excluded from the measurement.
current: No post-write measurement exists on any writer. `handleRemember` writes and returns success unconditionally — `packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/remember.ts:90-91` is `appendMemory(filePath, memory);` then `return successResponse(`Saved memory to ${filePath}`);`; its only guards are `memoryEnabled` (:77-79), empty memory (:80-83) and unresolvable scope (:85-88). The writer `appendMemory` (remember.ts:39-49) reads, formats, atomically renames and returns `void`. `successResponse` (packages/session-tools-core/src/response.ts:13-19) adds nothing, and `errorResponse` (:41-47) only prefixes `[ERROR]`; there is no third "write succeeded but…" shape. The sibling writer behind the UI RPC is identical: `appendMemoryFile` (packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:122-132), called from `appendMemoryForSession` (packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:80), measures nothing. The only limit constant in the subsystem is `MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200` (memory-store.ts:8); `grep -ran` over packages/ and apps/ for a 25KB byte limit, "read limit" or "memory index" returns nothing. That 200-line limit is applied only at LOAD, and only on the legacy fallback composer: `readMemoryFile` (memory-store.ts:29-33) slices to 200 lines and silently drops the rest, and `loadMemoryPromptBlock` (:317-334) is reached only when `capabilityContextPinned` is false (packages/shared/src/prompts/system.ts:453-455). On the live capability path there is no limit at all: `composePinnedCapabilityContext` pins each memory layer via `runtime.materializer.readText` (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:976-1015) and `readText` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/materializer.ts:169-186) reads the whole file. Neither loader strips YAML frontmatter or block-level HTML comments before slicing. The tool description the model reads before calling (packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:584, registered at :981) carries no conciseness, index or limit guidance. Two adjacent mechanisms exist and are NOT this one: `runScheduledAutoMemoryCleanup` (packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-cleanup.ts:260) is a daily, marker-scoped duplicate/age pass that never bounds the file, and the `trim_memory_files` suggestion (packages/pi-agent-server/src/context-categories.ts:239-247) fires on token SHARE via `isWorthAdvising`, is human-facing, and never reaches the model.
divergence: The entire synchronous post-write feedback loop is absent — this is not a key-name or value mismatch, there is nothing to rename. Three distinct pieces are missing: (1) no measurement of `MEMORY.md` after a write, so neither the near-limit reminder nor the over-limit error is ever produced on either writer; (2) the 25KB byte limit does not exist as a concept anywhere in the fork — only the 200-line one, and only as a load-time slice, never as a write-time check; (3) the documented measurement exclusion (YAML frontmatter and block-level HTML comments stripped before measuring) has no counterpart, because nothing measures. One rationale caveat matters for the fix: the doc's justification "everything past the limit is dropped on the next load" holds only on our legacy fallback composer (system.ts:453-455 → readMemoryFile's 200-line slice). On the shipped capability path nothing is dropped at all — the whole file is pinned every turn (base-agent.ts:976-1015 → materializer.ts:169-186), so the harm there is unbounded pinned-context growth rather than silent truncation. Both harms are real; a fix must decide which limit it is enforcing on which path.

change.symbol: MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT / new MEMORY_LOAD_BYTE_LIMIT, measureMemoryIndex, memoryIndexLimitNotice, readMemoryFile
change.what: Add `export const MEMORY_LOAD_BYTE_LIMIT = 25 * 1024;` beside MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT (:8). Add `export function measureMemoryIndex(content: string): { lines: number; bytes: number }` that first strips YAML frontmatter and block-level HTML comments (a `<!-- … -->` occupying whole lines — the trailing inline `<!-- nessy:auto:YYYY-MM-DD -->` marker written by remember.ts:21-25 is inline and must still count, matching Claude's rule) and then counts lines and UTF-8 bytes of what remains. Add `export function memoryIndexLimitNotice(filePath: string, m: { lines: number; bytes: number }): { level: 'ok' | 'near' | 'over'; message: string }` so both writers emit byte-identical text; model the over-limit message on errors.md:1440 (state that the write succeeded, name the file, the measured count, the limit crossed, and a rewrite target). Extend `readMemoryFile` (:29-33) to stop at MEMORY_LOAD_BYTE_LIMIT as well as maxLines, so what is measured is what is actually loaded.

After `appendMemory(filePath, memory)` at :90, re-read the file, call measureMemoryIndex + memoryIndexLimitNotice, and branch instead of the unconditional success at :91: `over` → `errorResponse(notice.message)` (the write already happened and the message must say so — the `[ERROR]` prefix is acceptable and is the only signal that survives the Codex/Responses path, see response.ts:21-40); `near` → `successResponse(`Saved memory to ${filePath}. ${notice.message}`)`; otherwise the current success string unchanged. Because this fork has no memory DIRECTORY of topic files, the remedy sentence must point at what we do have: move detail into a sibling file and reference it with an `@path` import — `readMemoryFileWithImports` (memory-store.ts:66-110) applies the line cap per file, so a moved block genuinely leaves the index. Import `measureMemoryIndex`/`memoryIndexLimitNotice` from @nessy-agent/shared/agent/memory rather than duplicating the thresholds.
One line: append "Keep one line per entry; MEMORY.md only loads its first 200 lines / 25KB." so the model has the constraint before it writes, not only after.

Decide explicitly and record the decision. The documented signal is delivered to Claude, not to the user, so the minimal fix leaves this human-initiated path unchanged. Surfacing the notice here requires a new field on `MemoryAppendResult`, i.e. an RPC/wire shape change — keep that out of the first change unless a plan asks for it.

Two cases: over-limit (seed a >200-line MEMORY.md, assert the entry IS on disk AND the result is isError with the rewrite instruction) and near-limit (assert success plus the reminder). The file already exists with four cases at :36-105.

One case that a >25KB file is cut at the byte limit on load, and one that YAML frontmatter and a block-level HTML comment are excluded from measureMemoryIndex while a trailing inline auto-marker is not.

blastRadius: `readMemoryFile` (memory-store.ts:29) has callers at memory-store.ts:77 (readMemoryFileWithImports) and packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:427 (the import scan inside memoryFileRecords), so adding a byte cut changes what BOTH the legacy prompt block and capability import discovery see — that is the one part of this change that is not measurement-only. `loadMemoryPromptBlock` is covered by packages/shared/src/agent/memory/__tests__/memory-store.test.ts and packages/shared/src/prompts/__tests__/system.test.ts:90. `appendMemoryFile` is called from packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:80. The remember result crosses the tool-result boundary into both backends: response.ts:21-40 records that `isError: true` is invisible on the Codex/Responses path, so the message text must be self-describing. The pinned-block composer (base-agent.ts:976-1015) and the capability snapshot's revision/contentHash check (materializer.ts:169-186) read the same file but are untouched by a measurement-only fix. As scoped there is NO persistence-format and NO wire-schema change; the only place a wire change would enter is the RPC item above (MemoryAppendResult), which is a risk trigger in this repo and is deliberately excluded.
userImpact: Two different harms, by path, and neither is signalled anywhere. On the shipped capability path (capabilityContextPinned true) nothing is dropped: MEMORY.md grows without bound and its whole content is pinned into every turn, so a long-lived workspace's memory silently consumes context and tokens, and the user's only clue is the /context overlay's generic `trim_memory_files` hint, which fires on token share rather than on the limit. On the legacy fallback path (prompts/system.ts:453-455) everything past line 200 is silently dropped at load, so a user who can see a fact in MEMORY.md gets an agent that has never read it — no error, no transcript note, no Memory-UI marker. Reaching either state today takes roughly 200 `remember` calls or a hand-edited long MEMORY.md, so for most users it is latent; it surfaces first on shared project MEMORY.md files that people also edit by hand.
notes: Read in full: remember.ts, response.ts, memory-store.ts, tool-defs.ts:584/:981, base-agent.ts:940-1025, materializer.ts:155-200, native-sources.ts (memory records + memoryFileRecords), prompts/system.ts:450-458, server-core rpc/sessions.ts:30-90, context-categories.ts:230-247, plus the raw memory.md:384-388 and errors.md:1435-1453 via curl. Two things are judgement calls, not doc facts: (1) the NEAR threshold is not numerically specified anywhere — errors.md's "under 140 lines" is the rewrite TARGET after crossing, not the near trigger — so the trigger point is ours to pick; (2) the doc's remedy "move detail into topic files" has no direct analogue because this fork has no memory directory (session = <dataPath>/MEMORY.md, project = <cwd>/MEMORY.md, user = <configDir>/MEMORY.md), so the nearest real target is the `@path` import mechanism. I ran no tests and no build.
